cells.tense: You are holding several true things at once right now, and they are not fighting each other.
cells.ask: Write one line naming the direction you are already moving in, and one plain reason you trust it. Put it somewhere you'll see it this week.
cells.core:
You can hold more than one true thing at once, and it isn't tearing you. There is a lot you can see, and you can see it without needing the pile to argue itself down to a single answer. That steadiness isn't confusion on a good day — it's the thing working.

The direction is being followed too. You know what you're moving toward and you'd recognize it without help; you've been steering by it without much fanfare. What this balance is free to feed next is structure: saying what you're aiming at out loud, plainly, so the people around it can line up with it. The cost of holding it this way is that an unnamed direction stays yours alone to carry. Naming one gives up a little privacy and buys a lot of ordinary help.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering by something you already recognize.
cells.verb: holding many true perceptions at once and turning them toward a direction
cells.place: the pull toward what is genuinely wanted, remembered rather than handed over

cells.tense: You will keep waiting for the moment everything lines up before you let yourself move.
cells.ask: Pick one direction and take the next small step in it before the picture is complete. Let the step be enough without needing an answer for the rest.
cells.core:
You're waiting for the picture to be complete before you move. Every version gets held up against a future that would settle it — when the conditions line up, when the last piece lands, when you finally know enough to be sure. So nothing gets chosen, and you stay braced for a moment that hasn't been written yet.

The direction you actually want keeps getting examined instead of walked, and the waiting is starting to hide it. Holding many knowings at once is real; pushed this way it becomes a reason to postpone commitment indefinitely. Aspiration is something to steer by once it settles on one direction. It doesn't need every direction resolved first. One step in one of them, taken before you're certain, tells you more than another round of looking. What you're calling patience is the part that doesn't want to find out.

cells.tense: You used to say what you were aiming at, and you have stopped saying it.
cells.ask: Tell one person about something you want to build or move toward. Say what it is and why it matters. Let whatever they say back be part of it.
cells.core:
You used to know what you were aiming at, and somewhere along the way saying it out loud stopped being worth the risk. The pull didn't go anywhere. The offering of it did, and the door you're standing at is behind you now.

So you watch the light from a distance and follow whichever direction seems safest. What you can see is still there and it isn't getting used. What's empty is the line between what you want and anyone else knowing it. Vision gets its strength from being shared — the dreaming runs on experience that's been digested, and something about yours hasn't been. You don't have to feel like it first. Say one true thing about what you want to someone, plainly, and notice what it's like to hear it out of your own mouth.

cells.tense: You keep calling it undecided while your attention has been pointing one way.
cells.ask: Say out loud the direction you've been moving in. One sentence to one person, and let it stand as yours.
cells.core:
You've been moving toward something, and you describe it as though the decision were still open. Look at what you keep returning to, what you defend, where your attention goes without being asked. That points somewhere, and you've been calling it still thinking it over.

You call the pull something that arrived on its own, so the choice stays unclaimed. Knowing what you want is closer to remembering than to discovering. You don't have to build a case for it or explain why. Just say the one you keep coming back to, to someone who's earned hearing it. The debt is minor — a small piece of what you know that you've been signing over to circumstances. Saying it once settles it.

attempts.check: The record gives the seat as aspiration toward light and the card as holding many truths at once, but it never says what this person has been aspiring toward or which truths they carry, so I am describing the mechanism and leaving their content blank. A reader could reasonably say the actual ambition is something specific and I have missed it; if so, the ask still stands because it only asks for one named direction and one written reason. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line implying I can see the star they steer by — so I leave what they want unnamed and let them supply it.
